Mix the beef with a third of the garlic, half the cumin, half the parsley, the egg and salt and roll into small meatballs.
Cook the chicken with the onion, another third of the garlic, the remaining cumin, paprika, pepper, oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 700 ml water and the chickpeas and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the meatballs and simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the last of the garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Finish with parsley and lemon and serve with bread.
Fry the onions in the oil for 15 minutes until golden brown, remove, crush to a paste with a little yogurt.
Fry the whole spices in the same oil, add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and sear for 10 minutes.
Add the yogurt, chilli, coriander and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the onion paste and 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes until tender.
Stir in the garam masala and kewra water and simmer 5 minutes until the oil rises.
Rub the chicken with lemon juice, salt and chilli and leave 15 minutes.
Coat in yogurt mixed with ginger garlic paste, cumin, garam masala and oil and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Roast at 230°C on a rack for 30 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with onion, tomato and cucumber salad.
Fry the chicken in the oil in a karahi or wok for 8 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the ginger garlic paste and tomatoes and cover for 5 minutes until the skins loosen, then remove the skins.
Cook on high, mashing the tomatoes, with the spices and salt for 15 minutes.
Add the yogurt and cook until the oil separates.
Finish with ginger, green chillies, black pepper and coriander.
Mix the mince with onion, half the tomatoes, chillies, coriander, spices, anardana, cornflour, egg and salt.
Shape into large thin patties and press a slice of tomato onto each.
Shallow-fry for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Serve with cucumber and the remaining tomato as a salad.
Boil the lentils and beans in 1.2 l water for 60 minutes until very soft.
Fry the onion in half the butter for 8 minutes, add the ginger garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and cook until thick.
Add the lentils and simmer on low for 30 minutes, mashing slightly.
Stir in the remaining butter, cream and garam masala and season.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the ginger garlic paste and chicken and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cream, crushed fenugreek and green chillies and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with coriander and serve with naan.
Boil the beef and chana dal with ginger garlic paste, spices and salt in 500 ml water for 45 minutes until dry and soft.
Grind to a paste, mix in the egg and shape into patties.
Shallow-fry for 3 minutes per side until crisp.
Blend the mint, coriander, chillies, lemon juice and salt into a chutney.
Fill the buns with kebabs, chutney and onion rings.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the ginger garlic paste and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the trotters and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the water, cardamom and bay leaves, cover and simmer on very low heat for 5 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Stir in the garam masala and season.
Serve with coriander, ginger, lemon and naan.
Knead the mince with onion, ginger garlic paste, chillies, coriander, spices and salt for 3 minutes.
Press onto skewers in long sausages and chill for 20 minutes.
Grill for 10 minutes, turning and brushing with oil.
Blend the yogurt with mint and salt for the chutney.
Serve with warm naan, onion and chutney.
Fry the onions in the oil until deep golden and remove half.
Add the chicken, ginger garlic paste, tomatoes, yogurt, masala, chilli and salt and cook for 25 minutes until thick.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes and drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken with mint, coriander, chillies, fried onions, saffron milk and ghee.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes, then mix gently and serve.
Rub the chicken with turmeric and salt and fry until golden, then remove.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic and ginger.
In 3 tbsp of the oil, fry the paste with lemongrass, cinnamon and star anise for 8 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, ketchup, sugar and 200 ml water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and onion and simmer 10 minutes until coated.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and whole spices in the oil, add the spice powder mixed with water and cook 4 minutes.
Add the beef and cook for 5 minutes, then 600 ml water.
Add the potatoes and coconut milk and simmer for 25 minutes until tender.
Cook the roti canai in a dry pan until flaky and serve with the korma.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, ginger and galangal and fry in the oil with lemongrass for 8 minutes.
Add the beef and stir to coat, then the coconut milk, lime leaves and turmeric leaf.
Simmer uncovered for 2 hours, stirring more as it thickens.
Add the kerisik, tamarind, palm sugar and salt and cook for 30 minutes more until dark and almost dry.
Marinate the beef with turmeric, coriander, cumin, lemongrass, half the sugar and salt for 1 hour and thread on skewers.
Cook the rice very soft, press firmly into a tin, cool and cut into cubes for nasi impit.
Simmer the peanuts with chilli paste, tamarind, the remaining sugar and 300 ml water for 10 minutes.
Grill the skewers for 6 minutes, turning.
Serve the rice cubes with satay, peanut sauce, cucumber and onion.
Blend the dried shrimp, shallots and garlic and fry in the oil with curry powder and taucu for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and mashed sweet potato and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts and divide into bowls.
Pour over the gravy and top with eggs, tofu and lime.
Rub the chicken with salt, stuff with half the ginger and the spring onions and poach gently in water to cover for 40 minutes, then plunge into iced water.
Fry 3 garlic cloves and some ginger in the oil, add the rice, then cook in 600 ml of the chicken broth with pandan for 18 minutes.
Blend the chillies with the remaining garlic, lime juice, sugar, salt and broth for chilli sauce; pound the remaining ginger with salt and oil for ginger paste.
Brush the chicken with sesame oil and cut into pieces.
Serve with the rice, cucumber, dark soy, chilli sauce, ginger paste and bowls of broth.
soup spice powder (coriander, fennel, cumin, pepper)
Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger and fry in the oil with the whole spices for 3 minutes.
Add the spice powder mixed with water and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the beef and water and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the potatoes and carrots for 25 minutes and season.
Serve with fried shallots and coriander.
Fry the garlic and chilli paste in very hot oil for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and prawns and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and both soy sauces and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs and fold through.
Add the bean sprouts and chives, toss 1 minute and serve.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, galangal and shrimp paste and fry in the oil with lemongrass for 8 minutes.
Add 700 ml water, the tamarind, torch ginger and mint and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the okra and tomatoes for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer for 8 minutes.
Season with sugar and salt and serve with rice.
1 for the dough, 3 for the filling
Knead the flour, water, one egg and salt into a soft dough, coat with oil and rest 1 hour.
Fry the mince with one onion and curry powder for 8 minutes, cool, then mix with the remaining eggs, chopped onion and coriander.
Stretch each dough ball paper-thin, spread with filling and fold into a square parcel.
Fry in ghee for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Toss the red onion with vinegar, sugar and salt and serve alongside.
Mix the flour with 150 ml water and salt into a batter, stir in the prawns and fry spoonfuls for 4 minutes until crisp.
Simmer the peanuts, chilli paste, sugar, tamarind and 300 ml water for 10 minutes until thick for the gravy.
Arrange the cucumber and bean sprouts on plates.
Top with sliced fritters, potatoes, tofu and eggs.
Fry the garlic and chilli paste in the oil, add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, then the squid for 1 minute.
Add the noodles, ketchup and sweet soy and toss over high heat for 3 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs and mix in.
Add the greens and bean sprouts for 1 minute and serve with lime.
Mix the spice powder with a little water to a paste.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and whole spices in the oil, then add the paste for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, then the coconut milk, potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 25 minutes, then stir in the yogurt and cashews and cook 5 minutes.
Season and serve with steamed rice.
Fry the garlic and chilli paste in the oil for 1 minute, add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes and tofu and toss.
Add the noodles with ketchup and soy sauces and toss over high heat for 3 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs and mix through.
Add the bean sprouts and greens for 1 minute and serve with lime.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger and turmeric and fry in the oil with the coriander, lemongrass and whole spices for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and water and simmer for 40 minutes, then shred the chicken.
Blanch the vermicelli and bean sprouts and divide into bowls with the chicken.
Ladle over the broth, top with fried shallots and serve with sweet soy mixed with chopped chillies.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk, 200 ml water, pandan, lemongrass and salt for 18 minutes.
Rub the chicken with turmeric, chilli and salt and deep-fry for 12 minutes until crisp and cooked.
Fry the anchovies until crisp and remove.
For sambal, blend the chillies and shallots, fry in 3 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, add tamarind, sugar and half the anchovies.
Serve the rice with chicken, sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.
Poach the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes, shred and keep the stock.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, candlenuts, shrimp paste and spices and fry in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the stock, coconut milk and tofu puffs and simmer for 10 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Blanch the noodles, vermicelli and bean sprouts.
Divide into bowls, top with chicken and ladle over the hot laksa.
Poach the fish in 1.5 l water for 10 minutes, flake the flesh and keep the broth.
Blend the chillies, shallots, lemongrass, galangal and shrimp paste and simmer in the broth with tamarind and the torch ginger for 20 minutes.
Return the fish, season with sugar and salt.
Blanch the noodles and divide into bowls.
Ladle over the broth and top with cucumber, pineapple, onion and mint.
Fry the anchovies in the oil until crisp and remove.
Pound the chillies, shallots and garlic and fry in the same oil for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken for 4 minutes, then push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the rice and soy and toss over high heat for 4 minutes, then the water spinach for 1 minute.
Season and top with the crispy anchovies.
Blend the lemongrass and shallots with the spices, 2 tbsp sugar and salt and marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers and grill for 8 minutes, basting with oil.
Simmer the peanuts with chilli paste, tamarind, the remaining sugar and 300 ml water for 10 minutes.
Serve the skewers with peanut sauce, cucumber and onion.
Marinate the beef with garlic, spices, half the oil and salt for 20 minutes.
Layer the potatoes, onion and tomatoes in a baking tray and tuck the beef between them.
Mix the tomato paste with 300 ml water and pour over with the remaining oil.
Cover with foil and bake at 190°C for 60 minutes.
Uncover, bake 20 minutes more until golden and sprinkle with parsley.
Rub the lamb with ras el hanout, cinnamon, saffron and salt.
Cook with the onions and butter for 10 minutes.
Add 700 ml water, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the raisins, almonds and honey and cook for 25 minutes until thick and glossy.
Whisk the chickpea flour, water, oil, salt and cumin until smooth and leave 1 hour.
Pour into a greased tray about 3 cm deep.
Bake at 200°C for 45 minutes until firm and golden on top.
Slice and serve warm with harissa.
Brown the lamb with the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste and spices, then 2 l water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the carrots, turnips and cabbage and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini, pumpkin and chickpeas and cook for 15 minutes.
Steam the couscous over the broth twice, fluffing between, and rub in the butter.
Serve the couscous mounded with lamb and vegetables, with broth on the side.
Knead the semolina, flour, salt and water for 10 minutes into a smooth soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the onions slowly in 3 tbsp oil for 15 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes, harissa and spices and cook for 15 minutes until thick.
Divide the dough into 6, oil the surface and stretch each piece paper-thin.
Spread filling in the middle and fold into squares.
Cook on a hot griddle for 3 minutes per side, brush with butter and serve warm.
Brown the lamb with the onion and celery in the oil.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, spices, half the coriander and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Add 1.5 l water and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the frik and chickpeas and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Finish with the remaining coriander and mint and serve with lemon.
Cook the chicken with the onion, half the garlic, spices, olive oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 500 ml water and simmer for 35 minutes.
Fry the zucchini in the vegetable oil until golden and drain.
Crush the remaining garlic with the vinegar and stir into the sauce.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Mix the beef with half the onion, parsley, egg, half the garlic, cinnamon, pepper and salt.
Mound the filling on the artichoke bottoms and press on lightly.
Soften the remaining onion and garlic in the oil and butter, add 500 ml water, the chickpeas and salt.
Lay the artichokes in the sauce, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and simmer 5 minutes more, then serve with bread.
Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, oil, salt and half the cumin until smooth and rest 30 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs and pour into an oiled baking dish.
Bake at 200°C for 40 minutes until set with a golden top.
Cool slightly and cut into squares.
Serve tucked into baguette with harissa and the remaining cumin.
Fry the beef and onion with cinnamon, pepper and salt for 8 minutes and cool.
Mix with the potato, cheese and parsley.
Place a line of filling on each pastry sheet, fold in the sides and roll into cigars, sealing with egg.
Fry in hot oil for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain and serve warm with lemon or soup.
Cook the meat with the onion, spices, oil and salt for 10 minutes, add the tomato paste.
Add 1.2 l water and simmer for 45 minutes.
Toast the pasta in the butter until golden.
Add the pasta and chickpeas to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes until tender and saucy.
Serve with the meat and halved eggs on top.
rechta or fresh thin ribbon noodles
Cook the chicken with the onions, cinnamon, pepper, oil, butter and salt for 10 minutes without browning.
Add 1.5 l water and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the turnips and chickpeas and cook for 15 minutes.
Steam the noodles over the broth for 10 minutes, toss with a ladle of broth and steam again for 5 minutes.
Serve the noodles topped with chicken and vegetables and broth poured over.
Cook the lamb with the onions, cinnamon, saffron, butter and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 600 ml water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes.
Add the prunes, raisins and honey and simmer for 20 minutes until syrupy.
Stir in the orange blossom water and serve topped with almonds.
Make a soft dough with the semolina, water and salt, roll thin and cook as flat rounds in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side, then tear into small pieces.
Brown the chicken with the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 1.2 l water, the potatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 35 minutes, adding the zucchini for the last 10.
Steam the torn bread for 10 minutes and toss with the butter and some broth.
Pile the bread on a platter and top with the chicken, vegetables and plenty of sauce.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, spices, harissa and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Make four wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve in the pan with crusty bread.
Mix the beef with onion, parsley, half the cumin and caraway and salt and roll into small balls.
Cook the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes, paprika and remaining spices and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the meatballs, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Rub the semolina with 1 tsp salt and 3 tbsp oil, add the water and knead to a soft dough, then rest 20 minutes.
Brown the beef and onion in the remaining oil, add the tomato paste, spices and 800 ml water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes and cook for 25 minutes.
Pat the dough into two rounds 1 cm thick, prick and cook in a dry heavy pan for 6 minutes per side.
Serve the kesra in wedges with the stew and coriander.
Cook the chicken with the onion, garlic, turmeric, pepper, oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 600 ml water and the carrots and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and olives and simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk the flour with the lemon juice and a little sauce and stir in to thicken.
Simmer 5 minutes and finish with parsley.
Soften the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices, then 1.5 l water, carrots and turnips and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini and chickpeas and simmer 15 minutes.
Grill the merguez for 8 minutes, turning, until charred.
Steam the couscous twice over the broth, fluffing between, and rub in the butter.
Serve the couscous with the merguez, vegetables and broth.
